title: Four Tribes Awaken
description: Every living cell now belongs to one of four coloured tribes: Gold, Azure, Rose and Lime. Newborn cells join the tribe that most of their parents belong to, and fresh births glow brighter. You command Gold, so paint cells to spread your tribe. A tribe that dies out respawns as a small seed.
observation: The board is still plain Conway B3/S23 in uniform green: still lifes, blinkers and a few drifting gliders at about 7% density, all one colour. It is a blank, single-species world. The first step is to give it identity and conflict.

title: Raiders and Fertile Ground
description: Settled tribes now launch glider raids at their rivals, and outnumbered border cells defect to the stronger tribe. Green fertile soil seeps up across the empty ground, and any two neighbouring cells standing next to fertile soil can sprout a newborn there. Click anywhere to set a crosshair; Gold's raiders will fly toward it.
observation: The board has settled into a quiet, crystallised peace at about 3% density. Gold, Azure, Rose and Lime clusters sit as still lifes and blinkers, with Azure narrowly ahead, and almost nothing is moving. The tribes exist but don't interact, so the world needs pressure, resources and conflict to come alive again.

title: Great Beasts Roam
description: Shaggy beasts now wander the world grazing fertile soil, leaving fresh soil in their dung and trampling any cells in their path. A tribe that surrounds a beast with enough cells hunts it down, earning Glory, stable homesteads and a burst of rich soil. Click to set your crosshair: it also lures nearby beasts toward Gold.
observation: Four tribes are scattered over a dark field with mossy patches of fertile soil. Azure leads, Gold sits second and Rose and Lime trail. Gliders fly between colonies, but the soil is only scenery that tribes passively use. The world has people and land and needs wildlife: something that moves on its own, eats the land and can be fought over.

title: Totems and Nightfall
description: Five ancient Totems now stand in the wild. The tribe with the most cells around a Totem drains its rival's hold and claims it. A held Totem enriches the soil and raises homesteads for its owner, and earns Dominion every few seconds. The first tribe to reach 600 Dominion wins the Era. Day turns to night and back, and Totems glow through the dark. Paint Gold cells near a Totem to seize it.
observation: Four tribes are scattered in small clumps over a dark field of mossy soil. Azure leads, glider raids fly often, and four beasts graze freely. Not one beast has been hunted, because the tribes are too sparse to surround them. The world has conflict and an ecology but no shared goal, so the tribes need places worth fighting over.

title: Storms, Rain and Wildfire
description: Clouds now drift across the world on a shifting wind. Rain clouds soak the soil and douse flames. Thunderheads hurl lightning that sets fire to fertile ground. Wildfire spreads through rich soil and burns any cell it reaches, leaving grey ash that later regrows as lush soil. Grab a cloud and drag it to blow it where you want: a cloud you have dragged belongs to Gold, and its lightning only strikes rival tribes.
observation: Tick 8020: four tribes skirmish across dark, soil-green ground. Gold leads in population and is 8 points from winning the Era. Beasts roam, five Totems glow, and day turns to night. The world has societies and creatures but no sky or weather, so the ground itself never changes on its own.

title: Rise of the Chieftains
description: Each tribe now has a crowned Chieftain who marches across the world, turns nearby rival cells to its own tribe and plants banner homesteads. A Chieftain caught among rivals, burned by fire or beaten in a duel by a stronger rival chief falls, and its followers scatter to the victor. Click anywhere to march the Gold Chieftain there, and lead it into enemy lines with a strong escort.
observation: Four tribes sprawl across the board. Beasts graze, Totems glow through the dusk, and storm clouds drift overhead. Gold leads in numbers, but Azure and Lime lead in Dominion. The world has weather, fauna and territory, but the tribes are still faceless swarms with no leaders to rally behind.

title: Rivers, Floods and Fishing
description: Two great rivers now wind across the world. Their banks soak up water and turn lush, so tribes crowd along them. Water stops wildfire and drowns any cell that wades in, so tribes can cross only at stone fords. Every so often the rivers flood: they swallow the banks, then leave rich silt behind. Tribes living on the shore catch jumping fish. Once Gold has 5 🐟, click a river to build a Gold bridge.
observation: Four tribes, Chieftains, beasts, totems and storm clouds share an open plain. There are about 1000 cells, and Azure narrowly leads in population while Gold dominates the Totems. The land itself is still featureless: soil, ash and fire are the only terrain. The world is becoming a living landscape, and it needs geography that shapes where tribes settle and fight.
